title: Higher-Order Stirling Expansion
description: Formalizes the first correction term in Stirling's asymptotic expansion: n! ~ √(2πn)(n/e)^n(1 + 1/(12n) + O(1/n²)). Shows this eliminates an axiom.

meta.author: Stirling (1730), de Moivre (1733)
meta.assumptions: None. 0 axioms, 0 sorries. The full chain {log_one_plus_le_cubic, log_one_plus_ge_quartic, stirling_step_formula, stirling_step_upper, stirling_step_lower, telescoping helpers (inv_sq_le_telescope, inv_cube_le_telescope, inv_harmonic_le_sq, inv_cube_le_telescope2, inv_quad_le_telescope), partial-sum bounds (log_stirlingSeq_partial_upper/lower), stirling_first_correction, stirling_two_term_expansion, error_bound_from_correction} is fully proved. The final upper-half exp-Taylor bound is discharged via Real.exp_bound at degree n=2 (|L|≤1 → |exp L − (1+L)| ≤ 3·L²/4), combined with L² ≤ 1/n² (from 0 ≤ L ≤ 1/n) and the algebraic identity L − 1/(12n) ≤ 1/(2n²) (from L ≤ 1/(12(n−1)) + 1/(12(n−1)²)).
originalContributions: Stirling series coefficients a_0=1, a_1=1/12, a_2=1/288, a_3=-139/51840
stirlingPartial: truncated Stirling expansion at k terms

log_one_plus_le_cubic: proved log(1+x) ≤ x-x²/2+x³/3 for x>0 (derivative monotonicity)
log_one_plus_ge_quartic: proved x-x²/2+x³/3-x⁴/4 ≤ log(1+x) for x>0 (derivative monotonicity)
log_one_plus_le_quintic: proved log(1+x) ≤ x-x²/2+x³/3-x⁴/4+x⁵/5 for x>0 (derivative monotonicity, fifth-order; infrastructure for second Stirling correction term 1/(288n²))
Telescoping helpers (inv_sq_le_telescope, inv_cube_le_telescope, inv_harmonic_le_sq, inv_cube_le_telescope2, inv_quad_le_telescope) and partial-sum bounds (log_stirlingSeq_partial_upper/lower)

stirling_first_correction (fully proved): combines the partial-sum bounds with two limits (htend_diff for L = log(stirlingSeq n) − log(√π), htend_Gn for the lower-tail residual via Tendsto.div_atTop on each tail term), Real.exp_bound at degree 2 for the upper-half Taylor remainder |exp L − (1+L)| ≤ 3·L²/4, and the algebraic comparisons (n−2)(4n−3) ≥ 0 (for L − 1/(12n) ≤ 1/(2n²)) and (12(n−1)³ − n³) ≥ 0 (for the lower half). Yields C = 2.
stirling_two_term_expansion (fully proved from stirling_first_correction via the √(2πn) = √(2n)·√π split)

overview.historicalContext: James Stirling published 'Methodus Differentialis' in 1730, giving the asymptotic formula n! ~ √(2πn)(n/e)^n and the full asymptotic series with Bernoulli number coefficients. Abraham de Moivre independently arrived at the same formula in 1733, and the constant √(2π) was supplied by de Moivre (Stirling had initially left it implicit). The higher-order terms n! ~ √(2πn)(n/e)^n · (1 + 1/(12n) + 1/(288n²) − 139/(51840n³) + ...) were known to both Stirling and de Moivre. The coefficients are given by the Euler-Maclaurin formula: applying the summation formula to Σ_{k=1}^n log(k) = log(n!) yields the asymptotic series, with the k-th correction coefficient a_k = B_{2k}/(2k(2k−1)n^k) involving Bernoulli numbers B_{2k}. Leonhard Euler's contributions to the Maclaurin-Euler formula (1730s) provided the systematic tool for deriving these coefficients. In the 20th century, the Stirling series was understood as the asymptotic expansion of the log-Gamma function: log Γ(z) ~ (z−1/2)log(z) − z + (1/2)log(2π) + Σ B_{2k}/[2k(2k−1)z^{2k-1}]. Mathlib's formalization uses the Wallis product as the entry point for Stirling's formula, making the connection to Bernoulli numbers indirect.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the higher-order terms in the Stirling expansion and use them to eliminate the error bound axiom in StirlingFormula.lean.
overview.text: Formalizes the Stirling series coefficients and the first correction term 1/(12n), showing it implies the axiomatized error bound.
overview.proofStrategy:
Rather than invoke Euler-Maclaurin (which would require Bernoulli-number infrastructure absent from Mathlib), the file proves the first correction by a self-contained telescoping argument:
1. Define the Stirling series coefficients and the truncated partial sums.
2. Prove sharp polynomial bounds for log(1+x) (cubic upper, quartic lower, quintic upper) by the derivative-monotonicity method.
3. Rewrite the consecutive difference d_k = log(stirlingSeq k) − log(stirlingSeq(k+1)) into the closed form (k+1/2)·log(1+1/k) − 1, and sandwich it as 1/(12k²) ± lower-order using the log bounds.
4. Telescope the per-step bounds (via elementary rational inequalities) and pass to the limit stirlingSeq(n+M) → √π, sandwiching L = log(stirlingSeq n / √π) between explicit rational functions of n.
5. Since exp(L) = stirlingSeq(n)/√π, finish with Real.exp_bound at degree 2 to convert the bound on L into the bound |stirlingSeq(n)/√π − (1 + 1/(12n))| ≤ 2/n².
6. Derive the two-term expansion of n! and the error bound (replacing an axiom in StirlingFormula.lean) as corollaries. The whole development is machine-checked: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
keyInsights: The first correction is proved without Euler-Maclaurin. Mathlib defines stirlingSeq via the Wallis product, so instead of connecting Wallis convergence to Bernoulli coefficients, the file telescopes the consecutive differences d_k = (k+1/2)·log(1+1/k) − 1 directly — a fully elementary route that needs no Bernoulli-number infrastructure.

The derivative-monotonicity lemmas for log(1+x) are the reusable engine: each bound g(t) = (polynomial) − log(1+t) has g(0) = 0 and a derivative that simplifies to t^m/(1+t) ≥ 0, so g is monotone and nonnegative. The same three lines of reasoning give the cubic, quartic, and quintic bounds.

Reducing the global limit to a telescoping series is the structural pivot: log(stirlingSeq n / √π) = Σ_{k≥n} d_k, so a sharp per-step estimate d_k ≈ 1/(12k²) sums (via 1/(12k²) telescoping against 1/(12(k−1)) − 1/(12k)) to the leading 1/(12n) correction with an O(1/n²) remainder.

The final exp/log bridge is handled by Real.exp_bound at degree 2: because |L| ≤ 1/n ≤ 1, the Taylor remainder satisfies |exp L − (1+L)| ≤ 3L²/4 ≤ 3/(4n²), which combines with L − 1/(12n) ≤ 1/(2n²) to yield the clean constant C = 2.

The Bernoulli formula a_k = B_{2k}/(2k(2k−1)) gives a_1 = 1/12 from B_2 = 1/6 and explains the sign pattern of the series (the negative third term reflects B_4 = −1/30), even though the proof itself never needs Bernoulli numbers.

The practical accuracy of the 1/(12n) correction is remarkable: for n ≥ 2 the relative error is < 1/n², and at n = 10 the correction 1 + 1/120 ≈ 1.00833 already matches the true ratio 1.00834 to about four decimal digits.

The error bound that replaces the axiom stirling_error_bound_ge_2 collapses to a single algebraic inequality once the correction is in hand: (11n − 12)/(12n²) ≥ 0 for n ≥ 2, closed by ring + nlinarith — illustrating how one quantitative theorem can retire a previously assumed bound.

sections.title: Module Overview
sections.summary: Docstring, imports, and namespace. States the goal — formalize the first Stirling correction 1/(12n) and use it to eliminate an error-bound axiom — and notes the coefficients' Euler-Maclaurin origin.

sections.title: Part I: Stirling Series Coefficients
sections.summary: Defines stirlingCoeff with the first four coefficients (a_0=1, a_1=1/12, a_2=1/288, a_3=−139/51840) and proves the values hold by rfl.

sections.title: Part II: Truncated Stirling Series
sections.summary: Defines stirlingPartial k n = Σ_{i<k} a_i/n^i and proves S_1(n)=1 and S_2(n)=1+1/(12n).

sections.title: Part IIIa: Sharp Polynomial Bounds for log(1+x)
sections.summary: Three sharp bounds — cubic upper, quartic lower, quintic upper — each proved by the derivative-monotonicity method: g(t)=(polynomial)−log(1+t) has g(0)=0 and g'(t)=t^m/(1+t)≥0.

sections.title: Part IIIa (cont.): The Stirling Step and Its Bounds
sections.summary: stirling_step_formula rewrites d_k = log(stirlingSeq k) − log(stirlingSeq(k+1)) as (k+1/2)·log(1+1/k)−1; stirling_step_upper/lower sandwich it as 1/(12k²) ± lower-order via the log bounds.

sections.title: Part IIIb: Telescoping Arithmetic Lemmas
sections.summary: Five elementary rational inequalities expressing each per-step bound as a difference of a potential function, so the partial sums telescope. Each reduces to nonnegativity of a polynomial numerator via field_simp + nlinarith.

sections.title: Part IIIc: Closed-Form Partial Sum Bounds
sections.summary: By induction on L, log(stirlingSeq n) − log(stirlingSeq(n+L)) is bounded above and below by telescoping potentials evaluated at the endpoints n and n+L.

sections.title: Part III: Main Theorem — Stirling's First Correction
sections.summary: stirling_first_correction proves |stirlingSeq(n)/√π − (1 + 1/(12n))| ≤ 2/n² for n ≥ 2. Takes L = log(stirlingSeq n/√π) = Σ_{k≥n} d_k, sandwiches L via the partial-sum bounds and the limit stirlingSeq(n+M)→√π, then converts to the ratio bound with Real.exp_bound. Fully proved, C = 2.

sections.title: Two-Term Expansion of n!
sections.summary: stirling_two_term_expansion restates the correction for n! itself, derived from the main theorem via the factorization √(2πn) = √(2n)·√π.

sections.title: Part IV: Error Bound (Replaces Axiom)
sections.summary: error_bound_from_correction derives stirlingSeq(n)/√π − 1 ≤ 1/n for n ≥ 2 — the statement axiomatized in StirlingFormula.lean. Reduces to (11n − 12)/(12n²) ≥ 0, closed by ring + nlinarith.

sections.title: Part V: Numerical Verification and Notes
sections.summary: Two norm_num checks anchor the correction at n=10 (1+1/120) and n=100 (1+1/1200), followed by development notes recording the path to 0 sorries and the iteration-5 addition of the quintic log bound.

crossReferences.description: Extends the basic Stirling formula with higher-order correction terms
The Gamma function extension also benefits from improved error bounds
The 1/(12n) correction sharpens the factorial estimates behind binomial-coefficient asymptotics, the analytic core of the de Moivre–Laplace local central limit theorem
The leading Stirling coefficient 1/12 comes from the Bernoulli number B_2 = 1/6 — the same constant that produces ζ(2) = π²/6 in the Basel problem

conclusion.summary: Proves the first correction term in Stirling's expansion: |stirlingSeq(n)/√π − (1 + 1/(12n))| ≤ 2/n² for n ≥ 2. The proof combines a Wallis-style telescoping argument (avoiding Euler-Maclaurin) with Mathlib's Real.exp_bound for the final exp-Taylor remainder. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: The first correction is fully verified (0 axioms, 0 sorries) and yields stirling_two_term_expansion and error_bound_from_correction by construction; in conjunction with StirlingFormula.lean (already verified) this gives a complete machine-checked proof of n!/[√(2πn)·(n/e)^n] = 1 + 1/(12n) + O(1/n²) with explicit constant C = 2. The proof method (telescoping bounds via the step formula d_k = (k+1/2)·log(1+1/k) − 1, plus log Taylor bounds via derivative monotonicity, plus Real.exp_bound at degree 2) is reusable: the same scaffolding applies to the next coefficient 1/(288n²), with one additional log-bound order needed. In probability theory, the first correction is essential for precise approximations of binomial coefficients via the local CLT and for bounding errors in Poisson approximation. The Stirling series (being asymptotic but divergent) is a classical example of an asymptotic expansion with Borel summability properties, connecting to the broader theory of divergent series.
